# GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — this is the concrete root cause behind one of the
"transient push-transport closes" that item asks us to retry. Retrying does not
help on its own: the connection is dropped with a *deterministic* trigger
(SSH idling for the duration of the suite), so every attempt fails the same way
and the agent loops, burning a full suite run each time.

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full` **after** `git` has
established the SSH connection to `github.com` and **before** the ref update.
The hook produces no SSH traffic for the whole run (measured 11 min warm, 35 min
cold on this host), so the remote closes the idle connection:

```
pre-push: full-suite gate for dev/main push — running run_tests.py --scope full ...
Connection to github.com closed by remote host.
pre-push: full suite green (cached runs make repeat pushes cheap)
pre-push: mirrored gate cache entry 96dd15da... into .worklog/cache
```

The gate reports **green**, the cache entries are mirrored — and the push never
lands: `git push` exits without updating the ref and `origin/dev` is unchanged.
Observed 2026-10-31 on two consecutive attempts from
`wl-LP-0MVWIA33O004RKP7-…` in `llm-manager`; `~/.ssh/config` sets no
`ServerAliveInterval`/`TCPKeepAlive`.

Impact:

- A green full-suite run is discarded, so the most expensive part of the push is
  paid repeatedly; because each retry rebases onto a moved `dev`, the tree
  changes and the suite cache misses, so retries are *cold*.
- The output reads as success ("full suite green") while the push silently did
  not happen — the misleading signal is arguably worse than a hard failure.

## Workaround that worked (not a fix)

```bash
GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20 -o TCPKeepAlive=yes" \
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev
# -> d925d89d..877a6512  HEAD -> dev
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dev push whose pre-push gate runs longer than the remote's idle timeout
      succeeds, with no manual `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` override by the agent.
- [ ] Keepalives are configured in a way that survives a fresh clone/worktree
      (e.g. set by the hook or by `implement.py`'s push, not only in one
      operator's `~/.ssh/config`).
- [ ] When the ref update is still lost after a green suite, the push reports a
      distinct, loud failure (not "full suite green" followed by silence), and
      distinguishes "suite red" from "transport lost".
- [ ] A regression test covers the transport-loss path (simulated closed
      connection) and asserts the distinct failure classification.

## Notes

- `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` / `SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN` (push must run from the worktree)
  is a separate defect; both were hit in the same session. This item is only the
  transport side.
- Related: `~/.ssh/config` on the multi-agent host currently has no
  `ServerAlive*` settings at all.

# Arrival-ordered turnstile in the shared semaphore

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC1, AC7). Implements the fairness half of the
starvation fix; the ordering tests come from the preceding test slice.

## Design (agreed direction — Q1 default (a), FIFO turnstile)

- A waiter takes a **monotonic ticket** in its namespace (a ticket file whose
  sequence comes from a flock-guarded counter), and **only the waiter holding
  the lowest outstanding ticket may attempt the slot scan**. Tickets are
  released on acquire, timeout, exception and crash.
- Ownership of a ticket is expressed as an exclusive `flock` on the ticket file
  itself, so the kernel releases it when the owner dies — a killed waiter's turn
  is reclaimed without PID bookkeeping and without stale state (crash-safety
  unchanged).
- The **fast path stays single-pass**: no outstanding lower ticket plus a free
  slot is one non-blocking scan, no ticket file written.
- Fairness is about *ordering*, not capacity: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` is
  untouched. Staggered-wait jitter (SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD) is kept — it
  complements ordering (distinct deadlines), it is not replaced by it.
- Fail-fast callers (`timeout=0`, e.g. `audit_runner`) are **not** queued: an
  immediate attempt is unordered by definition (it is not a waiter), so it must
  still succeed instantly when a slot is free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Semaphore.acquire()` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` grants a free slot to the oldest waiting arrival in its namespace (FIFO turnstile) instead of whichever waiter happens to poll next, so a waiter at queue position N is bounded by N × the expected hold time; the bound and the ordering contract are documented in the module docstring.
- [ ] Tickets are released on acquire, timeout, exception and crash (flock-backed, so a killed waiter's turn is reclaimed); no stale ticket can hold the queue.
- [ ] `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` is unchanged (ordering only, never capacity) and the staggered-wait jitter contract still holds.
- [ ] Fail-fast (`timeout=0`) callers still acquire immediately when a slot is free, and nested `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` namespaces stay isolated from the host-wide turnstile.
- [ ] The fairness, crash-reclaim, fail-fast and nested-isolation tests from the preceding test slice pass.
- [ ] The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the ticket layer to `Semaphore` (`_take_ticket`, `_ticket_is_head`,
   `_release_ticket`) with the turnstile consulted inside `acquire()`'s loop.
2. Reclaim abandoned tickets by attempting a non-blocking flock on the lowest
   ticket file and unlinking it when the owner is gone.
3. Update the module docstring: ordering contract, wait bound (N × expected
   hold time), crash-reclaim mechanism, fail-fast exemption, nested isolation.
4. Keep the audit-semaphore (`jitter=0.0`) and test-skill (`jitter=0.1`)
   call sites unchanged — no config or env churn.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — ticket/turnstile layer, docstring contract and wait bound
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — unit-level fairness and fast-path tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process ordering and crash-reclaim tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — slot-lane wrapper, unchanged (it is the main consumer)

## Constraints

- Do **not** change `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` or any ceiling.
- Keep the kernel-`flock` crash-safety property; no PID files, no daemons, no lock timeouts that can leave stale state.
- The turnstile must not add more than a couple of flock operations per attempt (a latency regression here multiplies across every suite run).
- Repository boundaries: framework source only; consumers receive it via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- Fair, starvation-bounded `Semaphore` with documented bound, plus green fairness tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the FIFO fairness test slice (which blocks this item).

# Bounded transport-close retry in git_push_to_dev

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (AC4, AC7). Implements the retry half of the
flake fix; the retry-policy tests come from the preceding test slice.

## Design (agreed direction — Q3 default)

- 3 attempts total (initial + 2 retries), jittered exponential backoff
  (~2 s, ~8 s, capped), retrying **only** the allowlisted transport patterns:
  `Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`,
  `remote end hung up unexpectedly`, `kex_exchange_identification`.
- Auth, branch-policy and every other error keeps today's behaviour;
  non-fast-forward keeps its existing dedicated rebase-and-retry recovery;
  `PushTimeoutError` is never retried (a timeout means the gate was running —
  replaying it multiplies cost).
- Every attempt uses the same cwd, argv and environment: the retry runs the
  pre-push hook again, which serves its cached full-suite entry. No bypass
  flag is ever injected.
- The attempt trail (count, backoff used, final reason) is logged and returned
  to the caller for reporting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Transient transport closes are retried with bounded backoff: `git_push_to_dev()` retries a transport-level close (`Connection to … closed by remote host`, `Connection reset by peer`, `remote end hung up unexpectedly`, `kex_exchange_identification`) up to a bounded number of attempts with jittered exponential backoff, from the **same cwd** as the first attempt.
- [ ] It fails fast (no retry) on auth, branch-policy and non-fast-forward errors, and never retries a push timeout.
- [ ] The retry does not bypass the gate: the pre-push hook runs again and serves its cached full-suite entry, and the attempt count, backoff and reason are logged and reported.
- [ ] The push cwd stays whatever the caller resolved — the retry reuses it and hard-codes nothing, so the push-from-worktree change can land without rework.
- [ ] The transport-retry tests from the preceding test slice pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a transport-close allowlist predicate and retry constants (attempts,
   backoff base, cap) with injectable overrides for tests.
2. Wrap the existing spawn/communicate logic in a bounded attempt loop,
   preserving process-group kill on timeout and the non-fast-forward detection.
3. Log each attempt (`attempt i/N`, reason, backoff) and carry the trail on the
   raised/reported failure.
4. No change to call sites' signatures (`-> bool` stays; richer failures are
   raised).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` transport allowlist, attempt loop and backoff
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — retry-policy tests (produced by the preceding test slice)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_abort.py` — finish interplay to keep green
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — non-fast-forward recovery must stay non-retried

## Constraints

- Only the recognised transport patterns retry — everything else fails as today (a retry must never mask a real error).
- Do not hard-code `repo_root` as the push cwd: reuse the caller's cwd (coordinate with SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN / SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3, which change it).
- Do not assume the keepalive fix (SA-0MVWNHLQQ002TFZR) has landed; the retry is the general safety net.
- UK English throughout.

## Deliverables

- A dev push that survives a transient transport close without a manual retry loop, with a visible attempt trail.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the transport-retry test slice.

# Live-repo guard fails a run when a concurrent `wl sync` moves `refs/heads/worklog/data`

## Target outcome

A full-suite run must not be failed — and must not lose its green cache entry —
because another agent's concurrent `wl sync` moved the Worklog data ref.

**Observed** while finishing SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS (2026-11-01):

```
run_tests.py --scope full → success: false
live-repo mutation detected: … moved ref refs/heads/worklog/data:
  0067d646089788ee530ff8856bd481d7bd1cd7c7 -> 96ea6f021c940ed2374e353de9f1df84f9438e6d
  (in the worktree AND in the main checkout)
```

Every test suite passed (`suites.all.returncode == 0`, 835/835 node tests, pytest
green), but the outer guard's verdict forces `success: false`, so no green
full-suite cache entry is written, and `implement.py finish`'s gate reports
"infrastructure reason" with no structured failures.

## Root cause

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` excludes `refs/worklog/*` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`)
from the mutation surface, but the Worklog data ref also lives — and moves —
under `refs/heads/worklog/data`. Concurrent `wl sync` (sibling `implement.py
finish` pushes, the herdr downtime worker) moves it while any suite runs, so the
guard reports it as a mutation of the guarded checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Excluded as concurrency churn.** `refs/heads/worklog/data`
  (and the `refs/heads/worklog/` namespace generally) is excluded from the
  live-repo mutation surface, derived from the ref name (never a work-item
  pattern), reported instead as an informational note.
- [ ] **AC2 — Regression pinned.** A test snapshots a fixture checkout, moves
  `refs/heads/worklog/data` externally, and asserts `_detect_live_repo_mutation`
  reports no mutation (note only).
- [ ] **AC3 — Suite-caused data movement still fails.** A suite that itself
  commits to `refs/heads/worklog/data` remains a mutation (the exclusion is
  provenance independent only if the guard cannot distinguish; if it cannot,
  document the blind spot explicitly in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`, mutation surface)
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` / `tests/test_guarded_roots.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Related work

- `discovered-from:SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS`
- WL-0MVPE2B8E005O0OS / SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — guarded-roots provenance work.

## Impact

Blocks any item whose finish requires a full-scope gate while other agents are
active: the green run cannot be cached, so `implement.py finish` cannot reach
its terminal status write, and audits see a cache miss.

## Goal

As the operator, I want the 2026-10-31 test-slot starvation fix proved shut with post-fix
measurements, and the remaining cross-consumer duplicate-suite vector removed, so that no agent
session loses minutes queueing for a 1–3 s test run and no two consumers pay twice for the same
full suite.

## Problem statement

The fast-lane fix (`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`, shipped `a2659c38` on 2026-10-31T23:21) delivered the
separate `test-fast` semaphore namespace, the re-derived `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 6` and
the `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane` reporting. Two gaps remain from the original RCA item
(`LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`, llm repo — closed as superseded by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`):

1. **No post-fix measurement.** Its AC5 ("median blocked time per work item falls materially below
   ~10 min/test call; evidence recorded") was never executed. A preliminary scan of the 30 pi
   session logs touched since `a2659c38` found 12 `slot_wait_seconds` samples, all `0.00 s`, and
   zero `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notices — encouraging, but too small a sample to close
   the question, and it says nothing about the two dominant wait categories (`implement finish` and
   the dev-push full-suite gate), which appear as `wait_for_job` blocks, not `run_tests.py` JSON.
2. **Verdicts are not reusable across consumers.** `run_cached()` keys on either the loose worktree
   fingerprint or — when the caller passes an explicit would-be-commit tree SHA — on
   `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. `implement.py` finish passes a tree SHA; the pre-push gate, the test
   CLI and the audit path pass nothing and therefore keep historical loose-worktree keys
   (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" says so outright). A green
   full-suite verdict therefore cannot be carried between the pre-commit staged tree and the pushed
   commit, so a dev push re-executes the full suite even when an identical tree was validated
   minutes earlier.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs evidence, not anecdotes, that the critical starvation fix worked:
  *As the operator, I want a recorded p50/p90/max of post-fix slot wait so I can close the RCA with
  data rather than with the fix's assertion.*
- **Agent session** — *As an agent pushing to `dev`, I want the gate to reuse a green verdict for
  the tree I am pushing so my push does not cost a second 7–9 minute suite run.*

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: two lanes
  (`test`, `test-fast`), ceilings 6 and 4, `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane`/`slot_lanes` reported,
  `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notice at ≥ 1 s.
- `skill/test_cache.py`: `compute_tree_state(index_file)` → `git write-tree` SHA;
  `run_cached(..., fingerprint=<sha>)` keys lookup and store with
  `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`; `query_cached()` stays worktree-only by design.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: finish no longer runs a full suite at all — it defers to
  the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`) and passes the tree SHA for its changed-scope verdict
  (`SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB`).
- `.githooks/pre-push` (SorraAgents, v3): full-suite gate runs
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` with **no** `--fingerprint`, i.e. worktree-keyed.
  It also **ignores the pushed `local_sha`** entirely (only `remote_ref` selects the gate), so the
  suite validates whatever the checkout happens to contain — there is no pushed-commit guard in
  this hook yet (the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook has one: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9`).
  `.githooks/pre-push.v2` (installed into other projects) deliberately has no suite gate, so it
  needs no change. Per-repo hooks diverge: `~/projects/llm/.githooks/pre-push` is a separate v4
  variant with its own pushed-commit guard and a `--project-root` argument.

## Desired change

1. Re-measure the post-fix wait distribution and record it (with the method) in this item.
2. Give the pre-push full-suite gate a pushed-commit guard and a tree-keyed fingerprint (plumbed
   through the runner CLI), so the gate measures the tree it pushes and its verdict lands in the
   same namespace as the finish gate's, and is reused when the tree matches.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Post-fix re-measurement recorded.** A reproducible analysis (commands/script cited in the item)
   over every pi session log covering at least 24 h after `a2659c38` (or all sessions since
   2026-10-31T23:21 if fewer) reports, per wait category — (a) `run_tests.py` slot wait, (b)
   `implement finish`, (c) dev-push full-suite gate — the call count and p50/p90/max wall clock.
   Pass: no run reports `slot_wait_seconds > 120 s`, partial-run (`test-fast`) p90 < 30 s, and no
   `queued N s` notice ≥ 30 s. Any miss is recorded honestly and filed as follow-up work, not
   smoothed over.
2. **The pre-push gate keys on the pushed tree.** The gate first adds the pushed-commit guard this
   hook currently lacks (pushed `local_sha` must equal the checkout's `HEAD` and the tree must be
   clean, with a loud refusal naming the commit, the HEAD, the tree path and the recovery step —
   the `llm` v4 hook's wording is the precedent), then computes that commit's tree SHA and passes
   it explicitly, so the verdict is stored and looked up with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. When the
   guard fails or the tree SHA cannot be computed the gate refuses rather than falling back to a
   loose worktree key (fail-closed, matching the cache's provenance contract).
3. **Cross-consumer reuse proven.** A test demonstrates that a full-suite verdict recorded for tree
   *T* by one caller (finish gate / tree-keyed `run_cached`) is served as a cache hit to the
   pre-push gate for the same *T*, and that a different tree misses. The gate reports cache
   hit/miss (and the reused entry's age) in its stderr/JSON output so a served verdict is visible.
4. **Runner CLI surface + docs.** `run_tests.py` accepts an explicit tree fingerprint for
   `--scope full` (the parameter already threads through `run_suite`/`run_all`), documented in
   `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` and the hook's header comment are
   updated — the "callers that pass nothing keep worktree keys … (test-skill CLI, audit, pre-push)"
   sentence must no longer describe the pre-push gate.
5. **Tests.** Deterministic tests cover: the gate computes and passes the pushed tree SHA; a
   same-tree second run is a hit; a different tree is a miss; fail-closed when `HEAD != local_sha`,
   when the tree is dirty, or when the tree SHA is unavailable; worktree-keyed callers' cache keys
   are unchanged byte for byte. Existing cache/provenance, finish-gate-tree and pre-push hook tests
   stay green.
6. **Rollout is explicit, not implicit.** The item records that the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook
   needs its own change (follow-up item), and that `pre-push.v2` consumers are unaffected.
7. **Testing/validation criterion.** Every new behaviour above is exercised by an automated test
   that fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Repository scope:** implementation lands in this repo only (`skill/test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, docs, tests). The `llm` repo's v4 hook is
  a follow-up in that repo; `ContextHub` and others receive `pre-push.v2` (no suite gate) and need
  nothing.
- **No synthetic saturation.** Measurement must be read-only log analysis; the host is live and a
  synthetic burst would manufacture the very contention being measured (same deliberate scope
  decision as `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`).
- **Cache correctness first.** Never degrade to a state-independent fallback key and never serve a
  tree verdict for a different tree; an unfingerprintable run simply executes fresh.
- **POSIX `sh` hook.** No new dependency, no `bash`-isms in `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Test execution policy.** All test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); no ad-hoc
  `pytest` invocations.
- **Do not edit the pacer/lane semantics** delivered by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — this item only
  measures them and changes cache keying.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — tree-SHA helper usable from a committed (not just staged) state, plus the
  existing `fingerprint_kind` plumbing.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — CLI flag for an explicit tree fingerprint, threaded to
  `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — add the pushed-commit guard, compute `HEAD^{tree}`, pass it, report hit/miss.

## Problem

The guard snapshots the main checkout at Step 0.75 and verifies only at `pre_push` and `pre_worktree_removal`. Every pre-push abort (build failure, gate failure in JSON mode, retries exhausted, interactive user abort) returns before either verify point, so `verifies` is `[]` and foreign deletions in the main checkout go unreported (2026-10-31: 37 deletions, `verifies: []`).

## Scope

Introduce one failure-path helper in `phase_finish` and call it from every pre-push abort path:

- `_record_main_checkout_verify(stage, *, aborting: bool)` — runs `_verify_main_checkout` with the failure stage label (`build_failure`, `gate_failure`, `user_abort`, `refactor`), and when violations are found posts the loud `_main_checkout_guard_message` via `wl_add_comment` (naming every path, the actor evidence and the recovery command) **in addition to** the existing failure comment — never instead of it (fail loud, never silent).
- Wire it into: Step 2 build failure; Step 3 gate failure in `json_output` mode; Step 3 retries exhausted; Step 3 interactive `abort` choice.
- `guard["verdict"]` becomes `fail` when a failure-path verify finds violations, so the report is honest even though those paths already return without raising.
- **Refactor step (advisory):** `run_refactor` failure currently only logs a warning and continues. Record a `refactor` verify entry **report-only** — a violation found there is surfaced in the report and in a wl comment but does not abort, preserving today's non-gating refactor semantics. Document this decision in the code comment and in the item comment.
- Expose the verify stage list in the report docstring/constant so the docs item can reference it (`VERIFY_STAGES`-style constant or module docstring).

**Parent ACs restated verbatim below** (the plan's AC coverage review measures similarity against them); this item's own checks follow.

- **Failure-path verification.** When finish aborts before the push (gate failure, build failure, refactor failure, user abort) and the main-checkout snapshot shows foreign changes (deletions especially), the guard reports them loudly — naming every path and the concurrent-actor evidence — via a wl comment on the work item, leaving the item open. A regression test covers a foreign-deletion abort at the gate stage (`verifies` non-empty on failure paths).
- **No regression on benign concurrent churn.** All changed-scope tests pass; the finish gate stays green for a clean run (no false positives on benign concurrent churn — the SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG defect class must not regress).

- When a failure-path verify finds foreign paths, a wl comment names every offending path, the actor evidence and the recovery command, and the pre-existing failure comment is still posted (both comments, in order).

- The work item is left `open` on every abort path (unchanged), and no failure-path verify introduces a new abort for benign concurrent churn — a clean failure path keeps `verdict == "pass"`.

## Problem

Two attribution defects:

1. `_resolve_main_repo_root` trusts `state.repo_root` whenever it is not the worktree or inside it, so a state file pointing at a sibling checkout makes finish snapshot, fast-forward and push a foreign repository.
2. `_record_finish_own_churn` returns the raw `git diff --name-only before after` list from `repo_root`; nothing constrains those paths to the repo being finished or to churn actually observed in that checkout, and `_main_checkout_guard_violations` allow-lists any listed path with a non-deletion code.

## Scope

- **Fail-closed `repo_root`.** In `_resolve_main_repo_root`, derive `main = _get_repo_root(worktree_path)` (git common dir parent) and require `state.repo_root` to resolve to that same root. On mismatch: log a loud WARNING naming the rejected and derived roots and use the derived root — never the stated foreign value. Keep the existing stale-state rejection, and keep the current fallback (stated root, or cwd discovery) only when derivation is impossible (`_get_repo_root` returns `None`), with a warning. Never return a path outside the repo that owns the worktree.
- **Constrained `own_churn`.** In `_record_finish_own_churn`: resolve `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `--git-common-dir` for `repo_root` and refuse (return `[]` + warning) when they disagree with `repo_root`; drop every path that is absolute, contains `..`, or does not resolve inside `repo_root`; and intersect the diff list with the paths actually observed dirty in the finished checkout (pass the post-fast-forward snapshot in, or re-snapshot inside the helper). Report dropped/not-observed paths as a `not_observed` diagnostic in `report["steps"]["local_dev_fast_forward"]` — visible, never allow-listed.
- Only record `own_churn` when the fast-forward actually advanced the checkout (`method == "advanced"`); a refused/no-op fast-forward contributes an empty list.
- Keep the invariant that a deletion (`D`) is never allow-listed, and keep SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG's benign-concurrent-churn exclusion intact (no new false positives for a clean run).
- Document the contract in the affected docstrings (`_resolve_main_repo_root`, `_record_finish_own_churn`, `_main_checkout_guard_violations`).

- `_resolve_main_repo_root` returns the main checkout derived from the worktree whenever that is derivable, and never a stated `state.repo_root` that disagrees with it; the mismatch produces a WARNING naming both paths.
- With an underivable main root (non-git worktree), the documented fallback + warning behaviour is unchanged (existing harness and tests stay green).
- `_record_finish_own_churn` returns only paths inside the finished repo that were observed dirty in that checkout after the fast-forward; foreign, absolute, escaping and not-observed paths are dropped and surfaced as a diagnostic, never allow-listed.
- A refused or no-op fast-forward yields an empty `own_churn`.
- Deletions remain never-allow-listed, and a clean finish still passes with no false-positive abort (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG).
- All tests from the sibling test item pass on the fixed tree and fail on the pre-fix tree; changed-scope gate green via `/skill:test`.

discovered-from:SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5

## Observed

During an epic `implement.py drive` run, the first driven child (**SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ**) was demoted from `in-progress` back to `open` by the herdr hydrator **four minutes into its implementation session**. The hydrator log:

```
2026-11-01T13:47:39.108Z [hydrator] released SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ: in-progress/intake_complete → open/intake_complete (no pane, claim holder dead)
```

and the item comment it wrote:

```
herdr-hydrator: released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: (none)
```

The child session was alive and working (it had already written its red test).

## Root cause (evidence)

The hydrator's `kept … live claim holder` rule (WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU) is *the* protection for pane-less driven sessions: it probes `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` for a live `flock`. But the lock is acquired inside the short-lived `implement.py start` **subprocess** and released when that process exits, so nothing holds the flock while the driven child session works. Measured while the session was alive:

```
$ cat .worklog/locks/child-SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ.lock
{"agent":"implement","pid":396636,…}      # pid 396636 already dead
$ fuser -v .worklog/locks/child-SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ.lock   # no holders
```

The spawned session's environment carries `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, but **no** `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN`, so the holder chain is broken at the `parent` → `start` → session boundary (the token is only propagated when the spawning process itself holds the lock, which `parent` does not).

## Impact

- A working driven child is reported `open` for the whole implementation: violates "actively worked ⇒ in_progress" and makes the herdr UI lie.
- `open` + a free lock makes the item **dispatchable again**: a second session can be spawned onto the same worktree (a second `phase_start` resumes it), i.e. two agents editing one tree.
- Every `drive`/`parent` run is exposed, since driven children are pane-less by construction.

## Desired fix (direction)

Make the driven session the lock holder for its own lifetime so the hydrator's live-claim-holder rule works as documented: either hold the `flock` in the long-lived driver for the child's duration **and** propagate the ownership token to the spawned session, or have the driven session acquire/hold the lock itself (re-entrant by token). The lock-file `pid` must name a live process, and `_probe_child_lock` must stay token-based (never pid-based).

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] While a driven child session is alive, `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is held by a live `flock` and the hydrator keeps the item `in-progress`.
- [ ] The spawned session receives `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` and its own `start`/`finish` re-enter instead of being refused (`skipped-held`).

# ship: CHANGELOG release section is discarded by the dev→main merge conflict resolution

**Origin:** observed in the `1916: The Rising` v0.1.23 release (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L). The Discord release notification went out with no release focus and no changelog body, and `main`'s `CHANGELOG.md` had no `## v0.1.23` section.

## Root cause

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` the CHANGELOG is generated **before** `origin/dev` is merged:

1. `generate-changelog.js "$NEW_VERSION"` writes `## v0.1.23 (…)` (with the `> **Release focus:** …` marker) and commits it on the release branch, which is based on `main`.
2. `git merge --no-ff origin/dev` then conflicts on `CHANGELOG.md`, because `dev` carries its own `## Unreleased` block.
3. The auto-resolution runs `git checkout --theirs CHANGELOG.md` — taking dev's whole file and **discarding the generated release section**.
4. The merged tree is tagged, so the released tree carries no `## v<version>` section.

The comment above the resolution (lines 217-219) even claims "generate-changelog.js rewrites it for the new version **afterwards**", contradicting the actual order.

Downstream effects:
- `discord-notify.js` `extractChangelogSection()` returns `null` and `extractReleaseFocus()` finds no marker, so the embed loses both the focus and the release notes (silently — only a focus warning is logged).
- Release notes are absent from `main`/`dev` for that version (recoverable only from the discarded commit).

## Proposed fix

1. Preserve the generated section across the merge: when `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts, take dev's version and then **re-insert** the generated `## v<version>` section (a small, tested helper), instead of discarding it.
2. Assert after the merge that a generated section is still present; abort the release (before tagging) if it was lost. A *failed generation* keeps today's non-fatal behaviour (warn and continue) — this only guards the regression where a successfully generated section is dropped.
3. `discord-notify.js`: log an explicit warning naming the version when no `## v<version>` section is found (still non-blocking).
4. Document the guarantee in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/changelog-merge.js` (new helper)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js`
- `skill/ship/tests/test_changelog_merge.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Acceptance criteria

1. With dev's `CHANGELOG.md` modified (an `## Unreleased` block present), the merge-resolution path yields a file that contains the generated `## v<version>` section with its `> **Release focus:**` marker **and** keeps dev's content — asserted by a node test over the new merge helper using a dev-style file.
2. When a section was generated but is missing after the merge, the release script aborts before tagging with an actionable message (non-zero exit) — asserted by a test of the resolution helper's "section lost" outcome plus the script-level guard.
3. A failed generation keeps the non-fatal contract: the release continues with an explicit warning, and the guard does not fire for a section that was never generated — asserted by a test.
4. `discord-notify.js` emits an explicit warning naming the version when the `## v<version>` section is absent, and still sends the notification (non-blocking) — unit test with an injected fetch.
5. The Discord embed still carries both the release focus and the changelog body when a generated section is present — unit test on the composition path.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documents the ordering/preservation guarantee and the abort-on-loss behaviour.

## Goal (user story)

*As an agent finishing a work item*, I need a slot waiter to take **any** free
slot in its namespace no matter how long it has been waiting, so a green change
is never blocked for hours while capacity sits idle (SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

`Semaphore._try_acquire_slot()` (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) probes
only `range(self.max_workers)`, and `max_workers` is resolved once in
`__init__`. A waiter that started when the pool held two slots therefore never
sees slots `2..7` created later by higher-ceiling processes — the observed
105-minute stall. The poll cadence is already bounded (50 ms base, jittered
`[0.5, 1.5]x`); there is **no** unbounded backoff in the shipped code. The
defect is the fixed-index probe.

This is the implementation slice; it turns the strict-`xfail` regressions from
the two test children green by removing their markers.

## Scope

`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`:

1. **Dynamic discovery.** Replace the `range(self.max_workers)` probe with a
   namespace scan: each attempt enumerates the numeric slot files currently
   present in the slot directory (deterministic ascending index order) and
   `flock`s the first free one. Slots created by a later, higher-ceiling
   process are therefore usable.
2. **Effective-ceiling rule.** The effective pool is the **union of slot files
   present** in the namespace; the caller's own `max_workers` is a *floor it
   guarantees* (it still creates `0..max_workers-1`), never a host-wide limit it
   may exceed. `_ensure_slots()` stays bounded by `max_workers`.
3. **Fail-fast stays fail-fast.** `timeout=0` performs one scan plus one
   `flock` attempt — no sleep, no blocking work added by the scan
   (`audit_runner` enters with `timeout=0`).
4. **Bounded cadence documented.** Keep the existing 50 ms base and jittered
   `[0.5, 1.5]x` retry; document the maximum poll interval (75 ms jittered, 50 ms
   unjittered) and that no backoff may grow without a documented cap. Record the
   measured directory-scan cost (a single `scandir()` of a directory with ~10
   entries) in the docstring or a comment.
5. **Docstring contract.** The module docstring documents the discovery rule,
   the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval.
6. **Preserve** the kernel-`flock` model (no PID bookkeeping, no stale locks, no
   daemon), jitter (`SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`) and nested-run isolation
   (`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`).

## Constraints

- **Do not change the configured ceiling.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` /
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics stay as shipped (`SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z`).
- **Do not implement ordering/fairness.** The FIFO turnstile is owned by
  `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`; the discovery scan must remain compatible with a future
  ticket layer (do not restructure acquisition into a queue).
- **Do not touch the `slot_busy` notice** — it keeps meaning genuine saturation.
- **Remove the strict `xfail` markers** added by the two test children as part of
  this slice.
- UK English; no ad-hoc suite invocations (`/skill:test`).

## Repo note

The affected code is this repository's framework source, consumed by other
projects via `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink. Run
`implement.py start SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` **from this checkout** so the worktree is
a SorraAgents worktree and `wl` resolves the `SA-*` item against this store.


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — discovery scan, effective-ceiling and poll-interval docstring contract.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — strict `xfail` markers removed; regressions green.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process regression green.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — saturation notice regression must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** A waiter whose ceiling is 2 acquires a free slot with index `>= 2` that already exists in the namespace, within one poll interval plus one `flock` attempt.
- **AC2** A waiter still creates at most its own `max_workers` slot files (`0..max_workers-1`); it never creates higher-index slots.
- **AC3** `timeout=0` remains fail-fast: exactly one scan plus one attempt, no sleep, no added blocking work (asserted by test).
- **AC4** The strict `xfail` markers from both test children are removed and all their assertions pass.
- **AC5** Jitter (`SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD`) and nested-run isolation (`SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86`) behaviour is unchanged — their existing tests still pass.
- **AC6** The module docstring documents the discovery rule, the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval (including the measured directory-scan cost); no backoff without a documented cap.
- **AC7** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` / `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics and the `slot_busy` notice are untouched; build plus changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC8** The full project test suite passes for the change (enforced by the dev-push gate; any gate-reported failure is triaged per the test-failure policy, not worked around).

> The block below restates the parent criteria this child satisfies (parent item
> SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0). It is the machine-checkable coverage mapping, not additional
> child criteria.

### Acceptance Criteria — parent coverage (restated)

- **Parent AC1** — Bounded acquisition once any slot in the namespace is free: a waiter that began polling when only slots 0..N-1 existed must acquire within a documented bound (one poll interval plus one flock attempt) as soon as any slot file in its namespace is free, including slot files created by a later, higher-ceiling process; a max_workers=2 waiter acquires one of the new slots created after it began polling, well inside its timeout.
- **Parent AC2** — Documented maximum poll interval, no unbounded backoff: the poll cadence has a documented maximum interval (50 ms base, jittered 0.5-1.5x when jitter is enabled) and a test pins that a long-waiting consumer still observes slots created after it began waiting (many poll cycles, not one); no backoff may grow without a documented cap.

## Goal

Make Phase 1, Phase 2 deep analysis and the verdict re-ask survive transient Local Proxy
connection failures (bounded, slot-aware retry) and, when they truly cannot, fail with an
actionable message that names the cause instead of a generic "Connection error." verdict.

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a large-context audit to either complete or
tell me exactly why it could not (phase, attempt count, elapsed, provider/pool cause), so a
transient proxy hiccup cannot permanently block a release with no diagnosis.

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

- The failing prompts measured 5.7–6.7 KB — smaller than a succeeding 6.3 KB sibling — and the
  exact captured prompt replays with HTTP 200 today. The "oversized request / truncate the
  payload" hypothesis is **not** supported.
- Retries failed in 11–387 ms (`stopReason: error`, "Connection error."), i.e. fast connection
  failures inside Pi's 2 s/4 s/8 s auto-retry budget, while the Local Proxy (3-slot pool) was
  serving another project's audit. `_PHASE2_MAX_RETRIES = 1` and the Phase-1 budget give no
  slot-aware backoff, and the verdict re-ask has no retry of its own.
- The provider-error path marks every AC `partial` with "Pi provider error: Connection error."
  and sets `ctx.script_failure`, which then triggers the Defect 2 persistence path.

## Scope

- Add a bounded, slot-aware recovery policy for provider *connection* errors in
  `phase2_deep`, `phase2_child`, `phase2_batch`, the Phase-1 parent/child screens and
  `verdict_reask`: a small number of retries with increasing backoff that yield the concurrency
  slot (so parallel audits do not retry-storm a saturated pool), capped so a single item cannot
  hang a release.
- Distinguish "proxy/pool unavailable" from a content/parse failure, and surface it in the
  report evidence with the phase, attempt count, elapsed seconds and the underlying error text.
- Give the emitted `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` a per-attempt identity (run id and/or started-at
  timestamp, appended to the stable key set) so an operator can always tell whether the numbers
  they are reading came from the attempt they just ran — and so a stale stored report cannot be
  mistaken for the current attempt.
- On exhaustion, the failure must be actionable: name the phase, the model/provider and the
  observed error, and state the remediation (re-run when the proxy pool has capacity,
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`, `--force`). Never mark an execution-dependent AC `met` on this path.
